name: Explosive Stick of Gann
summary: In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire turns stolen dwarven plans against Bael Modan. He built the charge to sabotage the dwarves’ flying machine.

sections.title: A Weapon of Retribution
sections.body: When Prospector Khazgorm led the Ironforge excavation into southern Kalimdor, the dwarves drove the Stonespire tauren from their ancestral village and razed their sacred grounds to build Bael Modan. Gann Stonespire reclaimed Khazgorm’s blueprints to avenge his displaced and fallen kin. He studied the plans and assembled a charge with enough force to wreck heavy machinery.

sections.title: Targeting the Sky Machine
sections.body: Gann made the explosive stick for the dwarven flying machine on an observation tower above the excavation. To him, the machine is more than transport or a weapon of war. It marks Alliance dominion over sacred tauren soil. Destroying it cripples the dwarven outpost and strikes a blow for the lost Stonespire tribe.

faq.q: What is the Explosive Stick of Gann?
faq.answer: Gann Stonespire crafted the explosive charge from recovered dwarven schematics to sabotage the Prospectors’ machinery on his ancestral lands.
Gann Stonespire assembled the explosive to avenge his tribe after the Ironforge dwarves at Bael Modan destroyed their village and desecrated their homeland in the southern Barrens.

faq.q: What is the explosive supposed to blow up?
faq.answer: The charge is meant to destroy the dwarven flying machine on a tower above the excavation at Bael Modan. Its destruction cripples the site's reconnaissance and brings symbolic revenge for the Stonespire tribe.

faq.q: How did a tauren learn to make dwarven explosives?
faq.answer: Gann built the stick from engineering blueprints recovered from Prospector Khazgorm, leader of the dwarven dig at Bael Modan. He turned the invaders’ own technology against them.

angles.text: As a tauren, using this weapon avenges the displaced Stonespire tribe and strikes back at the Prospectors who dug into sacred Kalimdor soil.
As an engineer, you can see how stolen blueprints turned against the dwarven machinery.
